sourceAtom.label: Identify surds
sourceAtom.visibleSubtitle: Determine whether these roots are surds

answer.worked: $3$ is positive and is not a perfect square, so $\sqrt{3}$ is irrational. Correct answer: Surd.
$\sqrt{3}$ is irrational, so multiplying it by the non-zero rational number $2$ leaves an irrational value. Correct answer: Surd.
$8$ is positive and is not a perfect square, so $\sqrt{8}$ is irrational. Correct answer: Surd.
$16$ is not a perfect cube, so $\sqrt[3]{16}$ is irrational. Correct answer: Surd.
$6$ is not a perfect cube, so $\sqrt[3]{6}$ is irrational. Correct answer: Surd.
$6$ is positive and is not a perfect square, so $\sqrt{6}$ is irrational. Correct answer: Surd.
$9$ is not a perfect cube, so $\sqrt[3]{9}$ is irrational. Correct answer: Surd.
The radicand $-1$ is negative, so $\sqrt{-1}$ has no real value. Correct answer: Not real.
$\sqrt{-1}$ has no real value; the minus sign outside the root does not change this. Correct answer: Not real.

sourceReview.taughtMethod: Evaluate perfect-square and perfect-cube roots; otherwise identify irrational roots, and reject negative square-root radicands as non-real.
